title: Engine History Analysis
summary: Designed and operated an Azure lakehouse for engine data, from streaming ingestion to tables ready for reporting.
contributions: Built batch and streaming pipelines on Azure Databricks and ADF.
Cut a critical PySpark job from 52 to 14 minutes and helped lower Azure costs by about 40%.
Led a four-person offshore team as Scrum Master.

Architected and owned ETL pipelines in Databricks Jobs & Pipelines (PySpark, Spark SQL) that process files through a Bronze/Silver/Gold Medallion Lakehouse on Delta Lake and ADLS Gen2, plus 7 production Azure Data Factory (ADF) pipelines for ingestion and ETL/ELT flows, modeling 50–60 Star Schema tables for Power BI.

Engineered streaming ingestion of 30–40 GB/day with Azure Event Hubs, Apache Kafka and Spark Structured Streaming, plus 5–7 GB/day of incremental batch loads using Auto Loader and SCD Type 2 Delta MERGE upserts, orchestrated through Databricks Jobs with daily Gold-layer refreshes.

Reduced a critical PySpark job's runtime by 73% (52 min to 14 min) and eliminated recurring executor out-of-memory failures by first applying selective key salting to a skewed join, then enabling and configuring Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) skew-join handling.

Lowered Azure platform costs by ~40% through right-sized Databricks job clusters, shorter job runtimes, Delta Lake OPTIMIZE and Z-ORDER with table partitioning, and parameterized, reusable ADF pipelines.

Built Python data quality checks (deduplication, null handling) into the Bronze and Silver layers, governed tables through Unity Catalog (RBAC, data lineage), and secured credentials with Azure Key Vault-backed secret scopes and service principals.

Deliver ~4 user stories and 2 bug fixes per sprint on feature branches merged into develop and main; prepare Azure DevOps YAML files and run CI/CD deployments of each branch to Dev for integration testing ahead of DevOps-owned promotion to Stage (limited-user UAT) and Production.

Lead a 4-member offshore team as Scrum Master across 27 two-week sprints and 3 production releases: daily stand-ups with UK client stakeholders, sprint planning on Azure DevOps Boards, mentoring 4 junior engineers and reviewing pull requests.
Use AI-assisted development (GitHub Copilot, Claude and ChatGPT in VS Code) to automate repetitive coding and test writing and raise code quality across the team.

title: Assumptions Management
summary: Built FastAPI data services and improved end-to-end processing with Redis caching and T-SQL tuning.
contributions: Built containerized FastAPI services with role-based access.
Cut processing time from 5–7 to 3–4 minutes with Redis and T-SQL tuning.
Maintained Pytest coverage and cleared SonarQube quality gates.

Developed containerized (Docker) FastAPI data services with RBAC and Azure API Management over Microsoft SQL Server and Azure Blob Storage; cut the web app's end-to-end processing time (including pipeline runs) from 5–7 min to 3–4 min via Redis caching and T-SQL query optimization.

Maintained 95–100% Pytest coverage on every branch and cleared all SonarQube quality-gate findings (reliability, security, maintainability, coverage, cognitive complexity) before merges to develop and main.
Early on, shadowed client technical walkthroughs and leadership reviews to learn the Rolls-Royce domain.
